Order a combination's products by reach, then marginal reach

Source: R/order.R
order_products.Rd

Orders the products of one combination greedily and reports how reach builds up one product at a time. The first product in products is kept first: in a turf() result it has the highest solo reach. Each later step adds the remaining product that reaches the most respondents not already reached. Ties are broken by solo reach, then by position in products.

Usage

order_products(df, products)

Arguments

df

A data frame of 0/1 activations, with one row per respondent and one column per product, as passed to turf().

products

A character vector of products (column names of df) in one combination, for example from extract_combination().

Value

A tibble with one row per product, in greedy order:

  • step: position in the order.

  • product: the product added at this step.

  • solo_reach: percent of respondents the product reaches alone.

  • marginal_reach: percent of respondents the product adds beyond the earlier steps.

  • total_reach: percent of respondents reached by this and all earlier steps. The last row equals the combination's reach.

  • frequency: total activations across this and all earlier steps, as a percent of respondents. Unlike reach, it can exceed 100.

Details

All measures are percentages of the respondents in df (0 to 100).

See also

extract_combination() to get products from a turf() result.

Examples

result <- turf(
  am,
  colnames(am),
  num_products = 4,
  batch_size = 2,
  keep_n_at_batch = 10,
  num_return = 3
)
#> Searched 4,358 combinations: 2,653 regular and 1,705 swap, across 2 batches.
order_products(am, extract_combination(result))
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>    step product   solo_reach marginal_reach total_reach frequency
#>   <int> <chr>          <dbl>          <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1     1 southwind       14.0          14.0         14.0      14.0
#> 2     2 coi             13.5          12.0         26.1      27.6
#> 3     3 lemon           13.5          10.6         36.7      41.1
#> 4     4 may             13.4           9.05        45.7      54.5
